content:
maya: Hey team — noticed a spike in 429s right after our auth token refresh window this morning. Users hammering endpoints for a few seconds then everything recovers. Anyone seen this pattern before?

maya: minimal log excerpt: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-Request-Id: abc123
Body: {"error":"rate_limited"}
```

alex: Yup — classic thundering herd when many clients refresh and immediately retry. If each client replays the same workload immediately you get a short burst of requests that trips rate limits. :grimacing:

tanner: Quick checks: are you using any idempotency keys for non-streaming generation calls? If not, retries might cause duplicate work and clients may be programmed to retry aggressively. Also check if clients back off with jitter.

maya: We only set Idempotency-Key in server-side queued jobs; client SDKs don't auto-add them for simple POST completions. Many web clients do immediate retry on network failure.

sara: Two angles: client-side policy + server hints. On the server we return Retry-After for 429 which is good. For client SDKs I recommend: 
- honor Retry-After strictly when present
- if 429 without Retry-After, treat as transient and use exponential backoff + full jitter
- always retry 5xx (except 501) with backoff

tanner: Agreed. Suggested backoff settings we use in other SDKs: 
```
initial = 200ms
multiplier = 2.0
max_delay = 60s
jitter = full (random between 0 and backoff)
max_attempts = 6
```
Small note: for streaming endpoints (server-sent tokens) we should NOT blindly re-POST if partial content was delivered — prefer resumable streams with resume_token.

alex: For 429 specifically: if Retry-After provided -> schedule retry after that header (plus small jitter). If no header -> apply exponential+jitter but cap attempts. And tag retries with Idempotency-Key for non-streaming endpoints so server can dedupe.

ci-bot: Related doc: https://redwood.internal/devex/retries (internal) — has examples for Node/Python backoff helpers.

maya: Language-specific: we have complaints from browser JS clients because token refresh is triggered by many tabs at once. Any advice for SDK behavior in browsers?

devex-lead: For browser SDKs: coordinate refresh across tabs via localStorage lock or BroadcastChannel. Also: when refresh completes, do NOT auto-replay all queued requests at once — drain with small randomized delays (e.g., 50-300ms). That smooths the burst.

sara: Implementation checklist for SDK teams: 
- honor Retry-After for 429s
- retry 5xx with exponential backoff + full jitter
- attach Idempotency-Key for idempotent-safe server dedupe on retryable operations (server supports it)
- streaming: support resume tokens, and only auto-retry resume where semantics allow
- browser: use cross-tab coordination for token refresh

tanner: Quick pseudo-code for backoff (Node): 
```
async function retry(fn){
  let attempt=0;
  while(attempt < 6){
    try{return await fn();}
    catch(e){
      if(!isRetryable(e)) throw e;
      let base = 200 * Math.pow(2, attempt);
      let wait = Math.random() * Math.min(base, 60000);
      await sleep(wait);
      attempt++;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max attempts');
}
```

alex: One more nuance — do not retry on 429 if the original request had side effects and no idempotency key. Surface a clear error to the app and let product decide. Automatic retries are safest for read-ish operations or when idempotency is present.

maya: OK thanks — I'll add these notes to the SDK issue and propose: default behavior = retry 5xx, retry 429 only when Retry-After or Idempotency-Key present, streaming resume supported, browser tab coordination for refresh. Will follow up with a PR for Node + browser libs. :+1:

devex-lead: Sounds good. Please include unit tests simulating concurrent refresh + burst to prove smoothing. If you need a test harness ping CI team.

maya: Will do — assigning to self, will open PR later today. Thanks all! :pray:
